## Notes

**Quick read:** Protected creator; a polished skit and voiceover editor who filmed her whole batch while pregnant (no child on camera) and is one of the best converters on the roster ($3,378 GMV, 52 orders, ROAS 1.82). She just gave birth (Sep 21).
**Best next move:** deliver the tailored angles and scripts pack Fatima promised on Sep 22, built around low-effort newborn and postpartum formats, and remind her gently the sling starts at 10 lbs so any newborn footage waits until baby is there.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- On camera: brunette mom with a messy top bun, black zip jacket over a pink crop top, filmed while visibly pregnant (bump in every sheet). Same setting every time: a plain bedroom or hallway with white doors, natural light. Her scripts call her a toddler mom ("Where my toddler mom is at?", "my toddler is stuck to my hip"), but no child ever appears.
- Format: voiceover plus on-screen text over B-roll, not a true yapper. Very expressive silent acting: grimacing and fighting a long grey striped stretchy wrap, then a smug smile as she slips on the Bambora sling, a close-up of the leather Bambora tag and buckle, the attachable phone pocket ("Cellphone holder!!!"), and a scrunched-up face as she balls up the old wrap at the end. About 24 to 33 seconds.
- Hooks (text): "When the wrap takes too long...", "When the wrap is too confusing...", "POV: Your toddler is stuck to your hip....", "POV: your toddler is stuck to your hip all day". Spoken hooks: "I hate struggling with my sling wrap all the time", "Where my toddler mom is at?". Everything closes on the sale: "They're having a massive sale right now", "It's a steal right now", "On SALE too!!".
- Batching style: one shoot cut into many variants (Aug 3 batch of 8 "different variations of on screen text hooks and captions", Aug 18 two re-edits where she moved the phone pocket earlier "to see if that might help increase the conversions"). She thinks like a performance marketer.
- What worked: 9 of 10 approved and all 9 ran as ads (a665b0f2, 3aa7d872, 96e3a4bf, 232e1099, 199dc731 each in 3 ads). 91 purchases, $5,851 purchase value on $3,219 spend. Her August videos were still selling in September.
- Rejected: 613fb34e only as a duplicate of 3aa7d872.
- Sheets: 613fb34e and 232e1099 frame sheets only captured 2 frames and 1 frame, the rest of those videos could not be read from the sheet (both are copies of the same script as 3aa7d872 and ba07efbd, which were fully checked).
- Safety and checklist: no child is worn in any video, so seat, M position and one-hand checks do not apply; it is really a product demo. Checklist 6 issue: word-by-word burned-in captions ("HATE", "SUPER", "THIS", "PRINT") on several variants, which the checklist now asks creators to avoid. The sale-heavy endings date fast.
- Strengths: the wrap versus sling contrast is her winning angle, great facial comedy, fast editing and willingness to iterate on hooks.
- To improve: now that she has a newborn, the next step is real wearing footage once baby is at least 10 lbs (with one hand on baby, seat under bottom, M position); and fewer "on sale" endings so the videos keep running.
